notes.title: Release Week Excitement + Dev Updates
notes.notes:
[p]It’s been a nearly a month since we flipped the switches—unfortunately, not literal switches—that released OFF on [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3339880/OFF/"]Steam[/url]! Before we get into anything else, we’d like to thank all of you who have followed the rerelease since our first announcement for your support.[/p][p]It’s been a real pleasure to see people reacting to something we’ve been working on for such a long time; we’ve spent a fair amount of time on our development channels sharing our favorite comments and posts with each other. (Steam reviews are a huge help as we move into the post-release phase of the game, and we’re really excited to have over 1,500 of them already.)[/p][p]That said, we’re not done using the development channels for development, either! We’re sending this newsletter to give you an early forecast of what’s coming next.[/p][h2]Roadmap: Languages[/h2][p]During our QA process, it became clear that the Spanish, Italian, and German language options weren’t quite ready to be released in their current state. We didn’t want to release these new localizations before they were ready, so we made the decision to temporarily remove them.[/p][p]This happened very late in the process—not only after we mentioned them in this newsletter, but sufficiently late that a few outlets reviewed the game with the incomplete language options in place.[/p][p]We’d like to sincerely apologize to anyone who purchased the game earlier than they intended because they’d read that the Spanish, Italian, and German options were already available. Our top priority right now is to get these options ready to go and back into the game; that will happen as soon as they’ve been completed and retested, and we’ll provide updates as that process continues.[/p][p]We’re also aware of some missing text in the game’s English and French scripts, including updated credits and transcriptions of the library books in French and Wide Angle messages for new enemies in both languages. At this point we’ve already addressed the bulk of those issues, along with a few typos and and missing punctuation marks in the French script; you should see all the fixes in our next update.[/p][p]If you’ve noticed something else that’s missing, or some other typographical error, please feel free to [url="mailto:offtherpg@fangamer.com"]send us an email[/url] so we can add it to our list.[/p][p]A couple of stray language notes:[/p][list][*][p]Japanese was not part of our day-1 release plans, but things are still moving smoothly there; we’ll have more information on that in a future newsletter.[/p][/*][*][p]Brazil is responsible for the second-most OFF wishlists of any country, so we’re excited to announce that a Portuguese (BR) localization is already in the works![/p][/*][/list][h2]Roadmap: Bug Fixes[/h2][p]Some other bug fixes are also in development right now—some of what the team is working on includes issues like incorrect enemy types being displayed and issues with the game window capturing and hiding the mouse cursor when that behavior is unwanted. Because of the different processes involved, you might see these updates happen at slightly different times for each platform.[/p][p]We thought we’d end on one reported bug that might be receiving a battlefield promotion to Feature. It concerns a secret boss, so I’ll be vague: One of the bosses is capable of taking damage you deal to it, under certain conditions, and dealing it back to your party. Some of you noticed that if you heal under those same circumstances, the boss will heal you, too. Not our developers’ intended behavior (or the boss’s), but a fun reward for figuring out what’s going on.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45353912/bd4e4999ab7c30a7956623d2567c0f1d36867172.png"][/img][/p][h2]Soundtrack[/h2][p]It’s been very gratifying to see so many positive comments about the new soundtrack; everyone who worked on it was very conscious of the lasting appeal and importance of Alias Conrad Coldwood’s soundtrack and eager to create something that would do the game justice in its own way. If you’d like to listen again, it’s all currently available in [url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pdzVxnqz45E&list=PLFyVSm0bEJUPnRwFIGNMjKPJ14GZnwOwg"]this YouTube playlist[/url].[/p][p](We’ve gotten some questions from people who are interested in buying or streaming the soundtrack, which is also very gratifying! We aren’t yet sure where else the soundtrack will be available, but stay tuned here for more information.)[/p][p]The news portion of this newsletter is now over, but if you’re the kind of person who likes to read every line of dialogue in an RPG, we asked members of the game’s development team to tell us about their favorite OFF songs. Here’s their responses:[/p][h3]Ryan Alyea (Studio Director)[/h3][p][b]Favorite New Song:[/b] Just like in the battle, I love how “JUSTUS” just feels like a bizarro mirror version of White Meat.[/p][p][b]Favorite ACC Song:[/b] When developing OFF, a lot of what was playable was only Zone 0 and “Empty Warehouse (Out).” Really brings me back.[/p][h3]Jack Murphy (Programmer)[/h3][p][b]Favorite New Song:[/b] I just love how foreboding “Don’t Be Too Loud” is. Gives me the feeling of something hidden that is beginning to stir and strain against binds ready to give.[/p][p][b]Favorite ACC Song:[/b] In a soundtrack filled with so much unease and underlying dread, “A Stab of Happiness” stands out as a small respite of light-heartedness, even if it’s only paper thin. The amusement park was one of the first locations I worked on, and I had this playing on loop a lot of the time.[/p][h3]Ryan Van Dyke (Combat Design, Programmer)[/h3][p][b]Favorite New Song:[/b] “WHITE ROT” captures the frantic energy of the Batter’s mission in a way that resonates really well—you kinda dig it, but it’s also very obviously messed up in its own right. The point that the song kicks in is, for me, when you start to really question if this mission is as pure as we're led to believe.[/p][p][b]Favorite ACC Song:[/b] “Fake Orchestra” stands out to me for being... almost nostalgic. It reminds me very much of the mid-2000s midi covers you'd find on VGMusic, but with more modern elements. The synths and experimental sounds stand out to me as being reminiscent of genres closer to metal, but when contrasted against the... flutes? some other type of wind instrument? found in this track, you really get a picture of Dedan doing what he does not because he CAN... but because he must.[/p][h3]Dan Moore (Script Supervisor)[/h3][p][b]Favorite New Song:[/b] I’m a sucker for the swell in “PHOENIX” as the drums come in; it really seems to fit with the way Japhet sees himself, and the way he reveals his true self as he realizes he’s doomed.[/p][p][b]Favorite ACC Song:[/b] The way the vinyl surface noise (is that what it is?) in “Windows Licking” becomes the backbone of the song is such a cool example of the way ACC’s songs confuse your expectations the first time you hear them.[/p][h3]chess!! (Social Media, QA Support)[/h3][p][b]Favorite New Song:[/b] gotta be "DOORSLAM SFX \[EXTENDED]". morusque wasnt kidding - that door really does slam \[extended]!! honorable mention goes to "AFTER SWINGS, MORE RUNS", which i heard for many hours while playtesting and scribbling notes. you can never predict what songs you'll develop a weird fondness for when doing QA!![/p][p][b]Favorite ACC Song:[/b] probably "Flesh Maze Tango"... i've probably listened to that one on loop for cumulative days in my own time. love that forward momentum![/p][h3]Amelia Bone (QA Lead)[/h3][p][b]Favorite New Song:[/b] I love "CHAOS IS LIFE - MALEDICION." The samples feel so good on the brain, and the song travels through a bunch of really captivating phases that constantly keep me guessing.[/p][p][b]Favorite ACC Song:[/b] It might be “Brain Plague”? The bass textures are so crunchy, and it does a lot to mess with perception and set a tone in an already trippy part of the game.[/p][h3]Everdraed (Animation)[/h3][p][b]Favorite New Song:[/b] When I create a trailer I'll generally listen to the song for many many hours and allow it to form motion and narrative concepts in my head. This version of “HOUR HAND” came very late, and the moment Toby had it ready I immediately timed an animatic of Mortis's Dedan storyboard against it. 'Oh! This is going to work beautifully...'

That would then become the basis for SmallBu's incredible animation, what a joy to help bring to life! Having edited, scrubbed, played it back innumerable times, Dedan's screams and gesticulations synced to the chorus is burned into my brain forever.[/p][p][b]Favorite ACC Song:[/b] I mean, it can only be “Pepper Steak.” I've had it in my winamp playlist since 2011, I've probably listened to it on repeat for many days of time as I've worked on various projects including this one. It's an incredible driver, a chaotic march to finish your duty, the anthem of the righteously driven and sleep-deprived.

When the OFF remake first began I'd listen to “Pepper Steak” nonstop in the background and visualize countless playouts in my mind's eye: of how the project would manifest, of how tribulations would be overcome, of resplendent trailers that would draw in a new era of fans.

Trailers that ultimately could never exist... Truly one of my great sadnesses! But that longing and loss makes the song itself all the richer to me.[/p][h3]Robby Bisschop (Marketing and PR)[/h3][p][b]Favorite New Song:[/b] “Hour Hand” is epic. It makes the pixel graphics come to life through my imagination and was the kind of track where I could intentionally do bad in combat just to listen to it longer.[/p][p][b]Favorite ACC Song:[/b] “Pepper Steak.” It’s raw and unpredictable. The first time I heard this I never knew what twist to expect next. It's like listening to the wildest stories from someone who forgets which tale they were telling halfway, but they are each so interesting you don't really care that none of them ever really reached a conclusion.[/p]

notes.title: OFF (PC) Review
notes.notes:
Whether it’s the year 2008, or the year 2025, turn-based RPGs are normally 30+ hour affairs that will leave you exhausted by the time the credits roll. The grind, endless narrative context, and a massive hero complex with world saving consequences is what the genre defines as ‘a feature’. But what if I told you, you only needed 5-7 hours to play one of the greatest and thought-provoking RPGs ever crafted?

What if I told you, you probably never heard of it? What… if the game was less than $20 in this new $80 landscape? These all seem like pipe dreams, but they’re not for the restored version of Mortis Ghost’s OFF. OFF brings one of the most unsettling gaming experiences back to centre stage, complete with a new soundtrack and new boss encounters, but retains the same charm of the often overlooked 2008 original.

Undertale has become a household name since it launched, and developer TobyFox credits OFF for inspiring the ‘Megalovania.’ Undertale became popular due to its... Read more

notes.title: OFF Now Available!
notes.notes: [p]In 2008, I was 21 years old, and I threw a ball into the universe, never imagining it would return. A few years later, the ball came back, and it was several kilometers wide. It seems that since then, the ball has never stopped growing. With the Fangamer team, we are sending the ball back into space today.[/p][p align="start"]Thank you!! Thank you for playing my game for seventeen years, thank you for still playing it. Thank you for all the content you've produced: the theories, the images, the videos, the cosplays, the games, and everything else. Thank you forever!! My gratitude to the community, the players, the fans, the curious, is immense. My life would not have been the same without the wonderful reception you've given OFF all these years.[/p][p align="start"]The ball is coming back to you now. Old and new players, I hope you enjoy it![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45353912/dd2ee178b8670de5aaafb1c23ec028c03a79702f.png"][/img][/p][p]-----[/p][p]OFF is Now Available on Steam for digital download![/p][p]Our new launch trailer, featuring brand-new animation from SmallBu, is linked below.[/p][p][url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OcPOkexZkHA][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45353912/f795f4dc5964838c36e0ec28a01d1fd60ba45486.png"][/img][/url][/p]

notes.title: Post-Prologue Development Updates and More
notes.notes: [p]It’s been a little over a month since [url="https://offtherpg.com/newsletters/06-releasing-august-15/?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=off-newsletter07"]we announced OFF’s digital release date—August 15[/url]—and the team has spent that time hard at work on lots of polish and detail work that we think will show through in the finished game.[/p][p]Your feedback on the Prologue we released for Steam Next Fest has been a huge help for the development team during that process, both in finding issues to address and prioritizing them. With the release date approaching, [b]we plan to stop offering the demo beginning July 31[/b], rather than diverting dev time to keep it up to date with the final version of the game. Your saves will still transfer over, but a lot has changed! We hope you give Zone 1 another spin when the game is released, so you can see all the balance and polish updates the team has made with your help. (For more on the Prologue and how we’re using your feedback, [url="https://www.tumblr.com/mortisghost/785642328641732608/about-the-off-prologue"]you can read Mortis Ghost’s blog post[/url].)[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45353912/f691ca10b830a1f9fee8f27bd4a8695c1bbfeef1.gif"][/img][/p][p]You can see two updates made based on user feedback in this brief gif of the Dedan fight. 1: The crit animation now follows you through the menu, to suggest that you can use your incoming critical hit to power up any menu option, not just Attack. 2: Dedan’s powerful Hour Hand and Half Past attacks have always happened at set intervals, but the game never made the cadence of the fight legible to players. A ticking clock now lets you know how much time you have until another super-move arrives.[/p][p]Localization work has continued, too; as translations arrive from each of our localizers, we’ve been working to make sure the game looks right in every language. Since Japanese requires more bespoke text-box work it won’t be ready right away, but work on German, Italian, and Spanish is nearly complete.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45353912/ebb92c10a25657d6b2b5a54eba71bde99880fdd8.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45353912/6103cdfbc8d8c5a6b045164a223afc52d84efa05.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i]Already you can learn about proper metal-extraction techniques in multiple new languages[/i][/p][p]Locking in the digital release date of the game means we’ve been able to set up our timeline for everything downstream of that, especially the physical release. Based on our August 15 digital release, we’re planning for a street date in Q1 2026, which should also be when your standard and Bad Human Edition preorders arrive. (If you’ve moved since preordering the game, don’t worry—we’ll be conducting an address check before the games arrive at our office to make sure they end up in the right place.)[/p][p]One other piece of feedback we’ve been able to act on isn’t related to the Prologue—we’ve seen all the requests, and we’re currently looking into doing everything we’ll need to make an EU release of the Bad Human Edition of the game possible. Watch for more information in an upcoming newsletter.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45353912/d411a5e652c82833176dc288762efcf10faa77ea.jpg"][/img][/p][p]If you’re following OFF [url="https://bsky.app/profile/offtherpg.com"]on[/url] [url="https://instagram.com/offtherpg"]social[/url] [url="https://twitter.com/offtherpg"]media[/url] you already know whether that’s Cob or not… but since we don’t want to tease our newsletter subscribers I will say that the answer is “Oh, no you’re not. You’re someone else.”[/p][p]Finally, last month was also exciting for the team because we got to see our first wave of OFF merch ship out. It was great to see so many photos of the Judge plush out in the wild. (We were glad that so many of you noticed it had an extra meow, too.) There’s another wave of OFF merchandise in the design and pre-production phase right now, for after the game is released; check back in November to see what’s coming.[/p]

notes.title: OFF Releases August 15th!
notes.notes:
Well, here we are, the "special moment."

It's time to reveal the news you've all probably been waiting for. It's canonical: Dedan can't wink, or even close his eyes!! He sleeps with them wide open, yes!

I wish you all a very good day. I think the team has something important to tell you too, by the way.

notes.title: More soundtrack news with Nightmargin
notes.notes:
Hello!

Musical team of champions!! Toby Fox!! Morusque!! Niiiiightmargiiiiin!?? Yes indeed, [url=https://offtherpg.com/interviews/nightmargin/?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=steam&utm_campaign=off-newsletter04]Nightmargin, the co-creator of OneShot, joins the all-star gang of artists who composed tracks for the new version of OFF[/url]. What a pleasure to have her among us! Her team's unique game, imbued with a melancholic and eerie atmosphere, is a very obvious member of a cyber-family tree in which OFF has a place a few generations above. In a kind of metaphorical euphoria, one could say that Nightmargin, as creator, took the torch (or rather the Sun wink-wink) that I myself had filed by the wayside, to carry it further, on another road, into another dream.

I am honored and happy that she is among the contributors to the new version; it’s like a circle closing, a day rising after a long night, a cookie delicious again long after its expiration date. No, this last metaphor isn’t as good, I cancel it. I hope you enjoy the pieces she composed as much as I do.

I bid you farewell, and see you soon for more news as impactful as baseball bat hits.

notes.title: Quinn K. talks localization and game dev!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,

Today's focus is on the translation of the game, [url=https://offtherpg.com/interviews/quinn-k/?utm_source=steam&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=off-newsletter03]a task that has been carried out by Quinn for the three English-language versions to date[/url], and it is on her work that the Fangamer teams based themselves directly to produce this new version. Frankly, without her OFF would never have achieved a hundredth of the success it profits today, international big up to her, eternal thanks through the big underwater tubes that criss-cross our planet, may the echo of my gratitude never cease to resonate in them, in her direction. I would also like to take this opportunity to say a big thank you to all the volunteer translators at OFF, who had the determination, year after year, to transcribe the entire script of my little game in lots of languages that I don't understand anything about. Very seriously, I'll keep thanking you until my deathbed, my last thought will be for you before my final little wink.

Okay, I hope you're doing well, don't worry I'm not going to die right away, there's still a little work to do on the new version.

See you soon, I wave goodbyes to you.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45353912/3098bb63b4d773ada8e3226b0d235b6430d29757.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45353912/dd2ee178b8670de5aaafb1c23ec028c03a79702f.png[/img][/url]

-----

Hey everyone!

We had a few comments last week about the “missing meat” in the Zone 1 preview track. In the game, the meat version of No Precipitation is a separate track so we made a hidden link in the word “meat” in [url=https://offtherpg.com/interviews/morusque/?utm_source=steam&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=off-newsletter03]Morusque’s interview[/url] to the song. Only 97 views at the time of writing, so congrats to those of you that managed to find it!

Thank you very much to everyone helping out with the amazing number of wishlists we have received. Since this edition is about localization, we also have some additional localization news: we're happy to announce that [b]we are bringing OFF to three additional languages: Italian, German, and Spanish[/b]. Localization has already started, and we will announce availability sometime in the future.

On top of that, we have been hard at work adding additional Steam features. We now fully support Steam Cloud, Steam Achievements, and the virtual keyboard on the Steam Deck and Big Picture Mode. We're very excited about your support so far on Steam, and [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/3339880/OFF/]if you haven’t yet, please wishlist the game on Steam![/url]

Ryan Alyea
Fangamer

-----

Since this week’s interview spotlights Quinn K. and her hugely important work on the game’s English translations, I thought it might be interesting to look at some places the game’s English will and won’t be changing.

[b]Competence[/b]: If you’ve dug into the French version of OFF already, you might know that the French “Compétence” would generally be translated as “Skill” in this context. Like Quinn before us, we’ve kept “Competences”—it’s just too much a part of the OFF lexicon at this point.

[b]The Up-Children-Down[/b]: The titles of the library books were originally translated by a French-speaking friend of Mortis Ghost’s, rather than Quinn. In French, this bit of light reading about miasmic forces swarming around in the belly of the world is called “Les Enfants-Vers.” “Vers” is a preposition you can use to mean “toward” or “around,” but it also means worms, which seemed to make more sense in a swarming-around-in-the-belly context.

We asked Mortis about it and he confirmed that the up-children-down are actually [b]The Worm Children[/b].

[b]That’s Practical[/b]: I think everyone has a little bit of a prior OFF translation that’s stuck around in their head ever since they first played it. Mine is the Batter in 2.0 saying “This Add-On is fighting by my side… that’s practical.”

Quinn updated that to “That’s useful” for 3.0, but when it came time to write the product page copy for the [url=https://www.fangamer.com/products/the-batter-off-hat?utm_source=steam&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=off-newsletter03]Batter Hat[/url] it seemed like a perfect chance to include an easter egg for longtime OFF fans.

Dan Moore
Fangamer

notes.title: More new songs with Morusque!
notes.notes:
Hello officionados!

I hope you are doing well since the last newsletter.

[url=https://offtherpg.com/interviews/morusque/?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=steam&utm_campaign=newsletter02]Today we reveal one of the pieces composed by Morusque[/url], who took care of a large part of the ambient music related to the different places in the game. Just like for [url=https://offtherpg.com/interviews/tobyfox/?utm_source=newsletter&utm_medium=steam&utm_campaign=newsletter02]Toby Fox[/url], I'm extremely happy to have him in the team, and I love the compositions he made. He managed to transcribe with great accuracy the original atmospheres, adding just the little strange sparkle that was needed to give a new pleasure of discovery to each environment.

Morusque comes from the same obscure old school French-speaking video game creation forums as me, and I have loved his work for a really long time now. He's a great and weird artist, and there was one time when we didn't know each other in person he came to wake me up while I was taking a little nap at a video game festival somewhere in France, then we chatted a little bit and I was really happy to have met him. Isn't that a good story?

I'm really excited for you to discover all this new music, in addition to the other new features in this updated version. Thank you for your enthusiasm, and have a great day! See you soon!

notes.title: Toby Fox joins the OFF soundtrack
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! I hope you are well, I am very happy to say hello to you in this first newsletter. The feedback has been numerous and very enthusiastic since the announcement of the collaboration with Fangamer, and then of the new version of OFF, and it reassured me and made me very happy. Thank you for all your comments and kind messages!

[url=https://offtherpg.com/interviews/tobyfox/?utm_source=steam&utm_medium=announcement&utm_campaign=newsletter01]Today we announce the Toby Fox collaboration[/url] on the different combat themes of the new version. This is information that I couldn’t yet give during the presentation livestream, and it wasn’t easy to keep my mouth shut about it, because I am really proud and happy that he is participating in the project! I love his work obviously, and it’s very exciting to have him in the team, and for such an important role! The music he composed is, I think, really excellent, and I can’t wait for you to discover it in-game.

They obviously don’t aim to eclipse the original Alias Conrad Coldwood soundtrack, but you’ll see that they offer a fascinating alternative to it, completely respectful of the original atmosphere, while bringing something new and very impactful. I still have trouble not listening to certain themes on repeat.

Well that’s all for today, I’ll send you a kiss and see you next time. Good luck with the coldy-cold breath of winter!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45353912/dd2ee178b8670de5aaafb1c23ec028c03a79702f.png[/img]

Hey there everyone,

Thank you very much for the kind reception during the announcement last month! With your support, we have just reached 50k wishlists on Steam. It’s been a pleasure to watch old fans return to the game and new fans discover it.

We’ll have much more to talk about in the coming months as we get closer to release. Keep an eye on this space as we’ll be sending these newsletters periodically to provide development updates and make a few more announcements about what’s new in the game. In the meantime, if you have not yet, please [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/3339880/OFF/]wishlist us on Steam[/url]. Every wishlist helps!

Ryan Alyea
Fangamer
